comments.text:
Confirmed in nats-server v2.15.3 source and by test. Hub side: canSubscribeInternal (client.go ~3470) lets a wildcard subscription cross to a LEAF only if perms.sub.allow (= the uplink user's pub allow, swapped) Match()es it or, for wildcards, ReverseMatch()es it. reverseMatchLevel on '>' calls getAllNodes(l), which adds the l.pwc/l.fwc nodes themselves and recurses only into l.nodes, never into l.pwc.next / l.fwc.next. So the allowance 'ants.inbox.*.dev-a' is never found for 'ants.inbox.>' (nor 'ants.plan.*.

' for 'ants.plan.>', so plan interest never crossed, even with the human on the uplink). Local fix (commit 59035d2 on fleet/1at): Permissions::for_leaf adds, per persona, its sendable patterns with '*' replaced by the persona id (ants.inbox.dev-a.dev-a, ants.plan.dev-a.dev-a): literal subsets of what the patterns already allow, so nothing widens. Test in leaf.rs: dev-a-only uplink; direct bus::publish -> Stored::Hub and plan::publish(Some(0)) stored; dev-b (not on the uplink) still gets "no stream" at once (the leaf filters by the uplink's perms before forwarding); ANTS holds 2. Existing uplink creds need re-issuing (ants auth leaf). Upstream bug report draft (nats-io/nats-server): Title: Leafnode: hub wildcard interest not propagated when the leaf user's publish allow has '*' before its last token (ReverseMatch/getAllNodes skips pwc/fwc subtrees) Version: v2.15.3 Repro: hub.conf: port: 4222 leafnodes { port: 7422, authorization { users = [ { user: leaf, password: leaf, permissions: { publish: { allow: ["foo.*.bar"] }, subscribe: { allow: ["_INBOX.>"] } } } ] } } leaf.conf: port: 4223 leafnodes { remotes = [ { url: "nats://leaf:leaf@127.0.0.1:7422" } ] } 1. hub: nats -s nats://127.0.0.1:4222 sub 'foo.>' 2. leaf: nats -s nats://127.0.0.1:4223 pub foo.x.bar hi Result: nothing received on the hub (no LS+ for foo.> reaches the leaf; a request gets "no responders"). Adding the literal allow "foo.x.bar" makes it work; so does a hub sub on "foo.x.*" (literal path through reverseMatchLevel). Expected: foo.> interest crosses, since its subject space overlaps an allowed subject; the hub still checks each inbound LMSG against the permissions (leafMsgAllowed). Cause: server/sublist.go getAllNodes() adds l.pwc and l.fwc but does not recurse into l.pwc.next, so allowances below a '*' token are never reported by ReverseMatch for a '>' query. Suggested fix: in getAllNodes, `if l.pwc != nil { addNodeToResults(l.pwc, results); getAllNodes(l.pwc.next, results) }`.

description: nats-server 2.15.3 propagates the hub stream's interest (ants.inbox.>, ants.plan.>) to a leaf only if the uplink's publish allowances ReverseMatch it; ReverseMatch (sublist.go getAllNodes) misses allowances with '*' before the last token such as 'ants.inbox.*.dev-a'. Without human in the uplink credentials, a persona's direct publishes from the leaf find no stream and go through the outbox even with the uplink up (and before ants-0ul, failed outright unless a hub client had a narrower live subscription). Investigate: report upstream, or a different subject layout / extra allowance that matches without widening what the leaf may publish.
title: Let the hub stream's interest cross a leaf uplink without the human's allowances

acceptance_criteria: An ant can start a channel thread and remains identifiable as its creator across replies and restarts. An ant-created thread uses the configured escalation chain of its creating ant without a new coordinator role; delegated work has a documented and tested origin-chain selection rule. Empty or exhausted chains, cycles and hop-limit exhaustion reach the configured default human rather than looping among ants. Existing turn budgets, escalation timeouts and once-per-level renewal protections remain enforced across restarts. Channel owner assignment or transfer does not redirect thread escalation. Existing human-owned threads and legacy threads remain compatible. Focused tests cover creator propagation, origin distinct from the stuck ant, multi-level escalation, human fallback and restart recovery. README and affected canonical requirements describe the resulting behavior.

description: Support channel threads started by an ant with permanent creator attribution and escalation through the existing escalate_to chain of the creating ant, ending at the configured default human when the chain is exhausted. Do not introduce a separate coordinator role or make an ant a human owner. Channel ownership remains limited to channel management and does not determine thread escalation.
design: Reuse existing escalation machinery, including chain lookup, leader progression, visited-target protection, max_escalation_hops, timeouts, turn budgets and persisted escalation state. Keep creator attribution distinct from the existing human owner field; retain compatibility with stored threads lacking creator metadata. Existing requirements start escalation from the stuck ant, which can differ from the creating ant: explicitly define origin-chain selection for work delegated to another ant and update affected requirements through bd spec change before changing that behavior. Preserve established human-owned thread behavior and human-only allowance renewal rules. No change to channel mention/messenger wake rules is implied.
title: Ant-created channel threads: creator attribution and existing escalation chain

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-83337b62
comments.text:
Investigation (nats-server v2.15.3, no code changed; issue left open).

LAG. ANTS (bus.rs:184 stream_config) sets no duplicate_window, so the server default of 2 min applies. The hub's ANTS_IN pulls each outbox through a source consumer. When the uplink drops, the source goes stale after 10 s and the hub sends a consumer-create request, waiting up to 30 s for a reply (srcConsumerWaitTime). After each failure it retries after 10 s x fails, capped at 2 min (stream.go calculateRetryBackoff). On leaf reconnect the hub restarts stale sources at once (leafnode.go checkInternalSyncConsumers -> retryDisconnectedSyncConsumers), except while a create request is still in flight (si.sip). In that case the retry waits for the 30 s timeout plus the backoff. The ANTS_IN -> ANTS hop is local and takes milliseconds. Worst-case landing after the uplink returns: about 30 + 120 + 2 = 152 s. Measured by instrumenting outbox.rs the_hub_takes_what_a_leaf_kept_while_its_uplink_was_down (reload-based outages, direct path back in 0.1 s): outages of 0/15/90/150/200/300 s landed 0.1-0.3 s after reconnect; 45 s -> 13 s; 60 s -> 48 s; 120 s -> 48 s; 240 s -> 79 s.

DUPLICATES. (a) bus::store_acked (bus.rs:471) falls back to the outbox on TimedOut (async-nats default 5 s). If the hub stored the message but the ack was lost, the outbox copy lands after the outage plus up to 152 s. That gap is unbounded by any window but is rare: it needs the uplink to fail between store and ack, or a hub slower than 5 s while the uplink is up, and in the second case the source is active and dedupes within milliseconds. (b) Dead letter (ants-xyb): a redelivery after reconnect calls bury_kept -> bury_letter. If the outbox copy has not landed yet, that path stores dead-<seq> directly, and the outbox copy can follow up to about 150 s later, past 2 min. That gives 2 letters, and replaying both delivers the message twice. Readers have no dedupe by envelope id: Answered notes (attempts.rs:121) live only until the ack, and the live Seen (bus.rs:537) holds only the last 1024 messages.

CONSEQUENCES of a late duplicate. An inbox message gets a second harness turn in the same session and a second reply; reply-<ant>-<id> no longer dedupes outside the window. A reply to ask_agent arriving late becomes a 'late replies' prompt. A channel post wakes or triages every member daemon again, which is the costliest case. Plan, notes and inbox listings show the message twice, and a human message renews the escalation allowance again.

REORDERING only spans the reconnect lag (0.1 s typical, about 150 s worst). A message sent directly after reconnect can be answered before an older buffered one on the same thread: the daemon queue keeps arrival order (daemon.rs ~480-510), inbox.rs:79 sorts by stream seq, and channel 'seen' uses seq watermarks, which stay safe because a late post counts as unseen. Nothing breaks, it is only out of order.

RECOMMENDATION:
(1) Set duplicate_window on ANTS explicitly to 24h. Add it to stream_config and let init_stream upgrade existing streams; ensure_stream warns like it does for other upgrades. Update the 'two minutes' wording in bus.rs:456-460, outbox.rs:16, dead.rs:23 and the README/docs. 5 min would already cover the dead-letter case and timeouts while the uplink is up. 24h also covers ack-lost cases across overnight outages. Cost: about 150 B of dedupe map per message id in the window (ddentry + map slot + id string), around 1.5 MB at 10k messages/day, plus a rebuildDedupe scan of one day's messages when the hub restarts. The server rejects only windows above max_age (30 d) or a server limit. Msg ids reused on purpose stay correct: replay-<seq>, mention.<post>.<human> and webhook hashes are meant to dedupe, and replays use a fresh id.
(2) Do not reorder by envelope sent_at in the daemon. Clocks differ between machines, it would mean holding messages back, and the lag is short. Optionally sort human-facing listings (inbox, plan, thread) by sent_at.
(3) Optional upstream: report the skipped reconnect kick while si.sip to nats-server.

title: Bound reordering and late duplicates of buffered messages

description:
Headless agent teams on several machines talk to each other and to the human from a terminal, without SSH or inbound public ports.

Decided:
- Backbone: NATS + JetStream (durable inboxes, acks, redelivery) and NATS KV (roster, sessions). Replaces Buzz's relay.
- Transport is pluggable: Dev Tunnels (TCP), direct ws/wss, or an HTTPS fallback bridge. Agents always talk to a local NATS leaf node; only the leaf's uplink changes.
- Persona daemon (antsd) per machine drives agent harnesses over ACP (stdio JSON-RPC). Copilot CLI (copilot --acp) first.
- Memory efficiency: Rust, one 'ants' binary (CLI, daemon, MCP), tokio current-thread, harness processes capped and evicted when idle.
- Names: project ants; subjects under ants.; stream ANTS; KV ants_roster, ants_sessions.
Source: 'Headless Agent Communication Over Dev Tunnels' design discussion.
title: Architecture: NATS/JetStream backbone, persona daemon, ACP harnesses, Rust

description: Webhook ingress: events from outside services delivered to an ant or a channel.
title: Webhook ingress

'ants webhook serve' takes 'POST <path>/<webhook>' for each [[webhook]] of its config file (default ~/.ants/webhooks.toml) and delivers each event, as that webhook, only to its configured ant's inbox or channel, on a new thread owned by the human its config names, if any; the sender cannot choose the destination.

With public_url and an action secret, an approval notice carries one link per offered verdict, signed with HMAC-SHA256 over the ant, request id, stream sequence, verdict, human and the request's expiry; GET on '<path>/_approval' only shows the request and a confirm button, and POST stores the ApprovalDecision with the human's credentials as 'ants tools approve' does, refusing a wrong signature (403), an expired link (410) or an answered request (409).
A human's credentials may create, read and ack only its own notification consumer 'notify-<human>' on ANTS; other users' credentials cannot create it.

A [[human.notify]] sink with 'device' gets no notice while that device follows what the notice is about (tool requests for approvals, the inbox for escalations), while the human's other sinks still get it; a sink without 'device' gets every notice, unreadable presence counts as away, and 'ants webhook serve' refuses device sinks for credentials without presence rights.

A webhook request is authenticated, by an HMAC-SHA256 signature of the raw body or a bearer token compared in constant time, before anything is read from or stored on NATS; a failure answers 401 and stores nothing.

A webhook's credentials publish only 'ants.inbox.<ant>.<webhook>' and 'ants.chan.<channel>.<webhook>' for their destinations and the webhook's own keys in ants_webhooks, read only those keys and the entries of their channels, subscribe only the webhook's reply inboxes, and write neither ants_channels nor ants_humans; 'ants webhook serve' refuses credentials naming another user, a human's, or ones that do not allow the configured destination.

'ants webhook serve' answers 202 only after the hub's stream acknowledged the event, and 503 with Retry-After while NATS is unreachable or does not store it, keeping nothing locally; bodies are limited to 256 KiB (413), requests to 15 s and to 64 at once (503 beyond).

An event is identified by its configured id (a header, a JSON pointer or the body's SHA-256), published with Nats-Msg-Id 'webhook.<webhook>.<hash>' and recorded in KV ants_webhooks (created by 'ants init') for 7 days, so a retry in that time, also after an ingress restart, answers 200 with duplicate true and delivers nothing new.

A channel webhook's post mentions nobody, so the channel's messenger triages it, or the users its config lists, or with broadcast = true every member of the channel when the event is accepted; mentions are never taken from the event.
A webhook is no human: its messages and posts never renew a thread's turn budget or allowance, and escalations on its threads go to the owner its config names, else the daemon's default human.

An ant's reply to a webhook's message goes to the thread's owner as a reply to a human when the owner is a human, else nowhere: the daemon logs it and acks the message, and never sends it to the webhook's inbox.

'ants webhook serve' notifies each [[human]] of its config of pending tool requests and of escalations reaching its inbox through its ntfy, Slack or Telegram sinks, reading as that human its durable consumer 'notify-<human>' so several processes send each event once; requests already decided or expired are skipped, and a failing sink is logged without its URL or token and never stops the others.

description: Creating an agent today takes 'ants auth user' on the machine holding account.nk, copying the .creds, editing ~/.ants/config.toml by hand and running ants daemon. Make it one command on the agent's machine, without moving any seed.
design:
Design sketch:
- 'ants persona add NAME --workdir ... [harness, model, ...]' writes the [[persona]] entry and generates the persona's user NKey locally; the seed never leaves the machine.
- Credentials: the request carries only the public key. Signing needs account.nk, so the approver runs on the key machine (or a small signer service there). Two paths: (a) out of band: print the public key; 'ants auth user NAME --public-key U...' prints the JWT; 'ants persona add --jwt' completes the .creds; (b) over NATS: an enrollment credential (publish only ants.enroll.<name>, subscribe its reply) sends the request; 'ants enroll list/approve/reject' on the key machine signs and replies.
- Then the daemon picks up the persona (start it, or the running daemon reloads its config).
- Open: --js-domain and leaf uplink updates (ants auth leaf / ants leaf outbox) for the new persona; enrollment credential issuance and expiry; whether multi-human (ants-548b) humans may approve.
title: Enroll a persona from any machine: ants persona add

comments.text: Implemented on fleet/dupes (701cc7a). Design: new KV bucket ants_attempts (file, max_age 30 d like the stream, history 1), key <persona>.<stream seq>, value {message: envelope id, reply?}. A marker naming another envelope id is ignored (a recreated stream reuses sequences). Flow in handle()/answer(): read marker -> none: put started, prompt as sent; started: prompt with the [ants] cut-off warning prepended (every redelivery after a started attempt, failed/naked or crashed); replied: re-send the recorded reply and ack without prompting. After the prompt the reply is recorded in the marker BEFORE publishing; replies (and turn-budget escalations) are published with Nats-Msg-Id reply-<persona>-<seq> / escalation-<persona>-<seq>, so a re-send within the 2 min duplicate window stores nothing; beyond it the same envelope (same id) is stored again. Marker deleted after ack and after a dead letter. Overdue delivery with a recorded reply sends it instead of dead-lettering. In-memory in-hand guard (0mi.10) kept. Permissions: persona gets STREAM.INFO, DIRECT.GET and $KV put/delete on its own keys only; human creates the bucket (ants init). Upgrade: rerun ants init and reissue persona/leaf creds. Spec: ants-0mi.13. Residual window: a crash after the harness answered but before the reply is recorded re-prompts (with the warning).

description: A crash after a harness ran tools but before the ack redelivers the inbox message and replays the prompt, so external effects can repeat. Store a 'started' marker (persona + stream sequence) before prompting; a redelivery that finds one is prompted with a warning that tools may have already run (the harness session is resumed with session/load), and a message whose reply is already stored is acked without prompting again.
title: Warn a redelivered prompt that its first attempt may already have run tools
